variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory fields `placed` and `arrivals` as updated at this step. `placed` is space-separated color words (the word none when nothing has been placed); a color's count is the number of times its word appears, and none counts as zero for every color. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. `placed` here is the value as updated at this step: a step whose execution frames show a cube held and whose last frame shows the fingers about 100% open with nothing held counts that cube as placed, so choose C when every goal count is then met, even if cubes of the goal colors remain on the table, including one that reappeared near the bin after the release. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last word of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table). At the first decision step, where several goal-color cubes may be present with no arrival order to read, the working color is the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (equal counts: the one the goal names first); `arrivals` as written at this step begins with that color, nearest the bin first, so that is where the first pick goes. At every later step the goal's counts and naming order play no part in the choice of color. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the working color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step. New cubes genuinely appear on the table during the episode, so a detection that was absent from earlier frames is still a candidate, and one that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. Excluded, at every step including step #1: a bin echo, meaning a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was there at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step (a cube 30 px or more from the center that stays in place is real, and a cube of a not-yet-placed color that appeared mid-step and stayed put is a candidate wherever it lies); a release echo, meaning a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame (the first execution frame of this step with the fingers about 100% open and no held line) within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame, excluded however far it is from the bin; a detection already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step, or matching a carried `arrivals` entry within about 12 px, is not an echo; and a detection whose position tracks the gripper from frame to frame. Among several candidates, choose the one that comes first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px): the oracle picks the cube of the working color that has been on the table longest. Only when the candidates cannot be told apart by `arrivals` (none of them matches an entry) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color: with one goal-color cube in the scene, that cube; with several, the cube of the color with the smallest required count in the goal (equal counts: the color named first) that is nearest the bin's reported center while at least about 28 px from it; when two such cubes are within about 3 px of the same distance to the bin, the one with the larger x (the robot's left). If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else the cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not within 28 px of it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not within 28 px of the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Write the word none as this step's value only at the very first decision step, where the carried-in memory is blank and there are no execution steps at all. The value is plain color words separated by single spaces and nothing else: no brackets, no quotes, no commas. A carried-in none that comes with execution steps is appended to by the check below like any other value: the first appended color replaces none, so the step after the first placement writes a single word such as blue. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except after a two-part check applied in order: first, does any execution frame of this step contain an object line ending 'is held in the gripper'; second, does the scene at this decision step (the last listed frame) show the fingers about 100% open with no held line. If both hold, the oracle completed the put-into-bin subgoal: append one space and that held cube's color exactly once (if the carried-in value is none, replace it by the color). The gripper's position when the fingers opened is irrelevant (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center); fingers opening only to 67-99% in an intermediate frame are irrelevant; same-color detections that appear, shift a few px, or vanish on the table in those frames are irrelevant (detections near the opaque bin are echoes of the held cube or bin contents, not table cubes). None of these is a reason to skip the append. e.g. carried-in red becomes red red; carried-in blue blue after a held-then-released blue cube becomes blue blue blue. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Emit the value as bare words only; any brackets, quotes or commas make it a wrong value. e.g. blue blue blue green
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. The value is the color words separated by single spaces, with no brackets, quotes or commas; at step #1 it is the word none. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. That held-then-released event is always one completed bin placement: count it regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. Example sequence over an episode: none -> none -> green -> green -> green green. e.g. blue blue blue green

fields.name: arrivals
fields.description: Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the subgoal rule picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames): if exactly one goal-color cube is in the scene, the list is that cube. If several are, the scene does not show which came first; list first every cube of the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (two colors needing the same count: the one the goal names first), then the next color by count; the order the goal names the colors is not the criterion. Within a color order by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping any detection within about 28 px of that center; when two cubes of one color are within about 3 px of the same distance, put the one with the larger x (the robot's left) first. Example with a goal of three blue and one green, green at [65, 109] and blue at [84, 112]: [[65, 109], [84, 112]]. A cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed. At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) PICK-UP REMOVAL, only if some execution frame of this step shows the fingers about 100% open over a table cube and a later frame of this step shows them at about 46% with a cube then reported held: remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in the frame where the fingers first reached 46%. If the very first execution frame already shows a cube held (fingers 46%, a held line), this is a put-into-bin step and nothing is removed, whatever entry lies near the gripper. Never remove an entry that still matches a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame; never stretch the 12 px test to the nearest entry. (2) RETAIN AND REFRESH: match one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each remaining entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new (handled in (3)). A matched entry is kept and set to that position; this match ignores the bin-echo and release-echo tests, which concern only new detections. Drop an entry with no such detection. (3) APPEND NEW: a goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended unless it is a bin echo or a release echo. A detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center is a bin echo only if it was present in the scene at the first decision step, or its color already appears in the carried `placed`, or this step released a cube of that color; a detection of a color not in `placed` that first appears in some execution frame of this step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the last frame is a genuine new cube however near the bin it is: append it, in the order of the frame where it first appeared. The release frame is the first execution frame of this step where the fingers are about 100% open with no held line; a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it. A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported in that frame, or that has moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame; it is excluded even when far from the bin center. A detection that was already at its place in the first execution frame of the step, or that matches a carried entry, is never an echo. A detection that appears mid-step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and stays put is a genuine new cube: append it. In a step that ends with a cube held (a pick-up step: first execution frame shows no held line, last frame shows one) there is no release frame, so the release-echo and moved-with-the-gripper tests do not apply; a new goal-color detection that appears near the gripper or near the just-grasped cube during such a step and is in the last frame is appended like any other, excluding only bin echoes. (4) When several new detections are appended, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared, earliest first, tracking each across frames within about 12 px; same-frame arrivals follow that frame's listing order. Order is otherwise never changed. Example: carried [[77, 139]], a pick-up step closing on [77, 139], with a red cube that appeared at [100, 66] several frames earlier far from bin and gripper, and two red detections within 28 px of the bin: write [[100, 66]]. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes currently lying on the table, in the order they first appeared in the episode, oldest first. Goal-color cubes are not all present at the start: new ones appear on the table while the robot works, and the oracle picks, within the color being worked, the one that has been on the table longest. At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene (a cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed). With one goal-color cube in the scene the list is that cube. With several, the scene gives no arrival order, so the annotator, reading the whole episode, lists first the pre-existing cubes the oracle actually picks during the episode in the order it picks them (first-picked first), and after them the never-picked cubes of a needed color ordered by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first (two within about 3 px of the same distance: larger x first), skipping detections within about 28 px of that center. At each later step, in order: (1) removal, only at a pick-up step (one whose execution frames show the fingers going from open to about 46% while the gripper is over a table cube, followed by a held line): remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in that closing frame. At a put-into-bin step, where the first execution frame already shows a cube held, remove nothing (the held cube's entry was already removed at its pick-up step). Never remove an entry that still has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; the 12 px test is never stretched to the nearest entry. (2) retention: matching is one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new. An entry with a match is kept and refreshed to that position; the bin-echo and release-echo exclusions do not apply here, so an entry matching a detection near the just-released cube's last reported position or near the gripper at release is kept. An entry with no such detection is dropped. (3) appending: every goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended, except bin echoes and release echoes. A bin echo is a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was present in the scene at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step; a detection of a color not yet in `placed` that first appears during the step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the scene at the decision step is a genuine new cube however near the bin it lies, and is appended in order of first appearance. The release frame is the first execution frame in which the fingers are about 100% open and no object line says held (a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it). A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appears in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moves a few px along with the retreating gripper over the following frames; it is never appended however far it is from the bin center. A detection is not an echo if it matches an existing entry within about 12 px or was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. A goal-color detection that appears during the step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and then stays put is a genuine new arrival and is appended. In a pick-up step (one that ends with a cube held and has no release frame) there is no release echo and no moved-with-the-gripper exclusion: every new goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that is not a bin echo is appended, even one within a dozen px of the gripper or of the just-grasped cube. (4) when several detections are appended in one step, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared (earliest first), tracking each across frames within about 12 px; two that first appear in the same frame follow that frame's listing order. Example over a step in which a green cube appeared at [86, 143] in an early frame and another at [86, 95] in a later frame, with [86, 119] picked up: [[86, 143], [86, 95]]. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]

field placed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as it is, with two points made literal so the written value and the policy's value coincide character for character. (1) The value is always written as a JSON array of double-quoted color strings, e.g. [] or ["green", "blue"]; at the first decision step of every episode the value is the literal [] (an explicit empty array, never a blank). (2) The append event is: the execution steps of this decision step contain at least one frame with a cube reported 'is held in the gripper', and the last frame of the step (the scene at the decision step) reports no held cube with the fingers about 100% open. That event is always one completed bin placement, regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames; append the held cube's color once. One example sequence over an episode: [] -> [] -> ["green"] -> ["green"] -> ["green", "green"].

field placed, POLICY PROMPT
  Three failures of PREDICTABILITY. First, at the first decision step (no execution steps, empty carried-in memory) the policy left the field blank where the annotation holds []; the instruction must say: when the carried-in memory is empty, write the literal [] as this step's value. Second, in most steps the policy produced the right colors but wrote them Python-style with single quotes; the instruction must say the value is a JSON array of double-quoted strings exactly like the carried-in value and the example, e.g. ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green']. Third, twice the policy declined to append because the release looked like a miss: the fingers opened with the gripper reported some 40-50 px from the bin's center, and in the same frames a cube of the held color was newly detected on the table near the release point. The instruction must say: the oracle always runs the put-into-bin subgoal to completion, so the pattern 'some execution frame of this step reports a cube held in the gripper, and the last frame reports no held cube with the fingers about 100% open' is always a successful placement; append the held cube's color once, whatever the gripper position at release and whatever cubes appear or move on the table. Value after such a step, e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"].

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Four things, in order of how often they broke SUFFICIENCY. (a) Reading the scene. Twice the policy, carrying an empty list and seeing many table cubes, chose a pick even though the last frame of the step reported a cube 'is held in the gripper' with the fingers 46% open and the gripper raised; it had read the earlier open-gripper frames. Rule 1 must say explicitly: the scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, and if any object line there ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46%), the answer is B before any other rule is considered. (b) Color priority. Rule 3's 'larger remaining count' is wrong and sent the policy to the other color three times. Every recorded episode with two goal colors finishes one color before starting the other: with placed=["green"] under a goal of three blue and two green, the next pick is green again; with placed=["green","green"] under a goal of two red and three green, the next pick is green again. Replace the rule with: if the last entry of `placed` is a color whose required count is not yet met, pick that color; otherwise pick any color that still has fewer entries than required. When `placed` is empty the recorded first choice does not follow the named order nor the larger or smaller count, so the rule should say any needed color is acceptable there. (c) Ghost and drifting detections. Twice the policy pointed at a detection that was not a real resting cube: once a cube of the needed color that first appeared exactly where the just-released cube had been held and whose coordinates shifted frame to frame, once a cube next to the gripper whose coordinates moved along with the gripper. The rule should say: a candidate must be reported as a table cube (not held) at the same coordinates, within about 2 px, in every execution frame of this decision step including the first one; a detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. (d) Tie-break among several stable cubes of the needed color. The instruction gives none, and the policy picked the first listed or an arbitrary one in seven steps. The recorded choices in this minibatch most often fall on the stable needed-color cube nearest the bin's reported center (in roughly three quarters of the cases), and never on a cube reported within about 25 px of the bin center, so the rule should say: among stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin but not overlapping it, and state that the point is the candidate's center as reported in the last frame, which may differ from any single listed coordinate by a pixel or two. The fallback clause 'nearest the gripper' should go, since the recorded picks are not nearest the gripper.

refused
  Several steps asked for one exact geometric rule that reproduces every recorded choice among same-color cubes (nearest the bin, largest y, image center, nearest the gripper). Read across the whole minibatch no single such rule holds: the nearest-bin preference fails in a few steps and every other candidate rule fails more often, so I pass nearest-bin on as a preference, not a guarantee, and do not pass on largest-y, image-center or gripper-nearest. One step asked whether a cube within about 30 px of the bin counts as on the bin; the one such case was also a ghost detection at the release point, so it is covered by the stability rule rather than a distance threshold. One step asked which color to start with when nothing has been placed yet; the three first picks in the minibatch go to the second-named color twice and the first-named once, to the color needing more once and fewer twice, so no rule is supported and I report only that any needed color is allowed there. One step suggested the recorded first-step point was a composite of several detections; it is within 2 px of a listed green cube, so that suggestion stays out.

New cubes genuinely appear on the table during the episode, so a detection that was absent from earlier frames is still a candidate, and one that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. Excluded, at every step including step #1: a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center (bin echo; a cube 30 px or more from the center that stays in place is real); a release echo, meaning a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame (the first execution frame of this step with the fingers about 100% open and no held line) within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame, excluded however far it is from the bin; a detection already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step, or matching a carried `arrivals` entry within about 12 px, is not an echo; and a detection whose position tracks the gripper from frame to frame. Among several candidates, choose the one that comes first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px): the oracle picks the cube of the working color that has been on the table longest. Only when the candidates cannot be told apart by `arrivals` (none of them matches an entry) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color: with one goal-color cube in the scene, that cube; with several, the cube of the color named first in the goal that is nearest the bin's reported center while at least about 28 px from it. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else the cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not within 28 px of it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not within 28 px of the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Write the word none as this step's value only at the very first decision step, where the carried-in memory is blank and there are no execution steps at all. The value is plain color words separated by single spaces and nothing else: no brackets, no quotes, no commas. A carried-in none that comes with execution steps is appended to by the check below like any other value: the first appended color replaces none, so the step after the first placement writes a single word such as blue. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except after a two-part check applied in order: first, does any execution frame of this step contain an object line ending 'is held in the gripper'; second, does the scene at this decision step (the last listed frame) show the fingers about 100% open with no held line. If both hold, the oracle completed the put-into-bin subgoal: append one space and that held cube's color exactly once (if the carried-in value is none, replace it by the color). The gripper's position when the fingers opened is irrelevant (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center); fingers opening only to 67-99% in an intermediate frame are irrelevant; same-color detections that appear, shift a few px, or vanish on the table in those frames are irrelevant (detections near the opaque bin are echoes of the held cube or bin contents, not table cubes). None of these is a reason to skip the append. e.g. carried-in red becomes red red; carried-in blue blue after a held-then-released blue cube becomes blue blue blue. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Emit the value as bare words only; any brackets, quotes or commas make it a wrong value. e.g. blue blue blue green
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. The value is the color words separated by single spaces, with no brackets, quotes or commas; at step #1 it is the word none. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. That held-then-released event is always one completed bin placement: count it regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. Example sequence over an episode: none -> none -> green -> green -> green green. e.g. blue blue blue green

fields.name: arrivals
fields.description: Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the subgoal rule picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames): if exactly one goal-color cube is in the scene, the list is that cube. If several are, the scene does not show which came first; list first the cubes of the color named first in the goal instruction, then the other goal color(s) in the order the goal names them, and within each color order by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping any detection within about 28 px of that center. A cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed. At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) PICK-UP REMOVAL, only if some execution frame of this step shows the fingers about 100% open over a table cube and a later frame of this step shows them at about 46% with a cube then reported held: remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in the frame where the fingers first reached 46%. If the very first execution frame already shows a cube held (fingers 46%, a held line), this is a put-into-bin step and nothing is removed, whatever entry lies near the gripper. Never remove an entry that still matches a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame; never stretch the 12 px test to the nearest entry. (2) RETAIN AND REFRESH: each remaining entry that has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame is kept and set to that position; this match ignores the bin-echo and release-echo tests, which concern only new detections. Drop an entry with no such detection. (3) APPEND NEW: a goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended unless it is a bin echo (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) or a release echo. The release frame is the first execution frame of this step where the fingers are about 100% open with no held line; a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it. A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported in that frame, or that has moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame; it is excluded even when far from the bin center. A detection that was already at its place in the first execution frame of the step, or that matches a carried entry, is never an echo. A detection that appears mid-step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and stays put is a genuine new cube: append it. (4) When several new detections are appended, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared, earliest first, tracking each across frames within about 12 px; same-frame arrivals follow that frame's listing order. Order is otherwise never changed. Example: carried [[77, 139]], a pick-up step closing on [77, 139], with a red cube that appeared at [100, 66] several frames earlier far from bin and gripper, and two red detections within 28 px of the bin: write [[100, 66]]. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes currently lying on the table, in the order they first appeared in the episode, oldest first. Goal-color cubes are not all present at the start: new ones appear on the table while the robot works, and the oracle picks, within the color being worked, the one that has been on the table longest. At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene (a cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed). With one goal-color cube in the scene the list is that cube. With several, the scene gives no arrival order, so the annotator, reading the whole episode, lists first the pre-existing cubes the oracle actually picks during the episode in the order it picks them (first-picked first), and after them the never-picked cubes of a needed color ordered by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping detections within about 28 px of that center. At each later step, in order: (1) removal, only at a pick-up step (one whose execution frames show the fingers going from open to about 46% while the gripper is over a table cube, followed by a held line): remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in that closing frame. At a put-into-bin step, where the first execution frame already shows a cube held, remove nothing (the held cube's entry was already removed at its pick-up step). Never remove an entry that still has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; the 12 px test is never stretched to the nearest entry. (2) retention: an entry that has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step is kept and refreshed to that position; the bin-echo and release-echo exclusions do not apply here, so an entry matching a detection near the just-released cube's last reported position or near the gripper at release is kept. An entry with no such detection is dropped. (3) appending: every goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended, except bin echoes (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) and release echoes. The release frame is the first execution frame in which the fingers are about 100% open and no object line says held (a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it). A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appears in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moves a few px along with the retreating gripper over the following frames; it is never appended however far it is from the bin center. A detection is not an echo if it matches an existing entry within about 12 px or was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. A goal-color detection that appears during the step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and then stays put is a genuine new arrival and is appended. (4) when several detections are appended in one step, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared (earliest first), tracking each across frames within about 12 px; two that first appear in the same frame follow that frame's listing order. Example over a step in which a green cube appeared at [86, 143] in an early frame and another at [86, 95] in a later frame, with [86, 119] picked up: [[86, 143], [86, 95]]. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
